warnings: CORRECTED 2026-08-09: a bug in the prior version of this file applied the terminal exit-multiple cap to terminal OWNER FCF instead of terminal EBITDAF, which caused the cap to bind far below the documented 12.5x/13.5x/10.5x multiples (the effective EBITDAF-basis multiples were only 8.2x/9.3x/6.1x). This has been fixed: the cap is now min(gordon_growth_tv, terminal_cap_multiple x Y10 adj_ebitdaf), consistent with Step 8c.5 and with how the historical EV/EBITDAF anchor multiples were computed. Base IV moved from $4.99 to $6.36; bull moved from $8.44 to $11.28 (now ABOVE the current price); bear moved from $1.90 to $2.57. See sanity_check for the re-run trip-condition analysis.

This is a component-built 10-YEAR owner-FCF model (not 5-year) because Contact is mid-way through a multi-billion-dollar renewable growth-capex supercycle (Manawa integration, Te Mihi Stage 2, Glenbrook-Ohurua battery, Kowhai Park & Glorit solar, Tauhara 2 pre-FID) that will not taper to a mature, capital-light run-rate within 5 years.

Historical per-share/equity CAGRs spanning the 11-Jul-2025 Manawa Energy acquisition (scrip+cash, shares 798.5m -> 994.4m) and the Feb-2026 NZ$525m equity raise (994.4m -> 1,054.4m) are NOT comparable pre/post-deal; equity CAGR is used only as a cross-check, not as the primary growth driver.
SBC is immaterial (~0.15% of revenue, ~$5m/yr) and is deducted for completeness but is not a material driver of the valuation gap.

inputs.net_debt_balance_sheet_date: 2025-12-31 (H1 FY2026), adjusted for Feb-2026 NZ$525m equity raise (proceeds added to cash, new shares added to count; raise post-dates the 31-Dec-2025 balance date)
inputs.interest_income_treatment_note: NOT stripped from FCF: Contact is a large NET-DEBT company (net debt ~$2.37bn post raise), not net cash, so the net-cash double-count rule (Step 1b-b) does not apply. Interest income ($11m FY2025) is immaterial relative to ~$180-280m/yr of interest expense on $3.2bn of debt.
inputs.sbc_source: 10-K/Annual Report FY2025 Note E8 'Share-based compensation' (Extracted/CEN.NZ_Annual_FY2025_FS.txt): FY2025 SBC expense $5m, FY2024 $4m -- confirmed immaterial, no equity-award tax withholding or buybacks disclosed (both verified 0)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 EBITDAF guidance (~$965m, +24.7% YoY on Manawa full-year consolidation) as Year-1 anchor, decelerating from ~4.5% to ~2.0% revenue growth over the 10-year horizon (base case) -- NOT equity CAGR or a single blended historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity (book value) CAGR is near-flat/negative (3yr -0.95%, 5yr +1.04%) versus double-digit Revenue (12.9%/10.6%) and EPS (21.1%/18.9%) CAGRs -- a >30-point divergence. This is NOT a red flag on earnings quality; it reflects that Contact has funded its capex supercycle predominantly with DEBT (net debt roughly doubled FY2023-H1FY2026) and dividends, not retained earnings, so book value has stayed flat even as revenue/EBITDAF/EPS grew. Equity CAGR is explicitly NOT used as the growth driver for this reason, and because the Manawa scrip issuance (798.5m->994.4m shares, 11-Jul-2025) makes any single-line equity CAGR spanning the deal date non-comparable pre/post-acquisition.
historical_growth.notes: Reported FCF CAGR is not computed/reported (None) because reported FCF is not meaningful across FY2022-2025 (43, -190, 0, 72 -- entirely a function of the growth-capex supercycle's timing, not underlying earnings quality). Underlying EBITDAF grew at a 15.9% 2-year CAGR (FY2023-25, the only years with a disclosed underlying figure) and is the best available cross-check for the guided FY2026 EBITDAF growth of +24.7% (Manawa full-year effect).

base.terminal_cap_multiple_basis: EV/Y10-EBITDAF, anchored to CEN's own FY2023-25 average EV/underlying-EBITDAF of ~12.84x
base.notes: Year-1 revenue/EBITDAF anchored to FY2026 guidance (~$965m EBITDAF on ~$3,258m implied revenue from the H1 FY2026 run-rate). Growth capex tapers from the committed $1.1bn under-construction programme (Te Mihi Stage 2 online CY2027, Glenbrook-Ohurua battery Q1 CY2026, Kowhai Park solar Q2 CY2026) plus the new Feb-2026-funded $540m tranche (Glenbrook battery 2.0, Glorit solar JV, Tauhara 2 pre-FID), fully tapering to stay-in-business-only capex by ~Year 8-9. Stay-in-business capex rises gradually from $110-130m (pre-Manawa run-rate) toward $158m to reflect the enlarged 30-hydro-scheme asset base. Terminal value: Gordon growth (12,675.9) binds ahead of the 12.5x EBITDAF cap (14,448.0) -- the cap is a backstop here, not the active constraint.

bull.terminal_cap_multiple_basis: EV/Y10-EBITDAF, at the top of CEN's own historical EV/underlying-EBITDAF range (FY2023 13.49x)
bull.notes: Electrification demand (Fonterra 540GWh/Steel EAF/data centres) exceeds MBIE reference case; Manawa synergies fully captured and de-risk hydrology; EA reform proves benign (no structural separation); renewable build completes on/ahead of schedule with capital-efficient synergy capex, allowing growth capex to taper faster than base case. Lower WACC reflects reduced regulatory-risk premium if EA reform outcome is benign. Terminal value: the 13.5x EBITDAF cap (19,787.4) now binds AHEAD of Gordon growth (20,673.3) -- the cap is the active constraint in this scenario, preventing the compounding of an above-consensus growth rate with a low WACC/terminal-growth spread into an unbounded valuation.

bear.terminal_cap_multiple_basis: EV/Y10-EBITDAF, below CEN's historical range to reflect a structurally impaired regulatory/hydrology environment
bear.notes: EA structural/operational separation materializes or is priced in via a persistently higher cost of capital; dry-year hydrology and continued NZ gas-supply decline compress margins and require more thermal/gas backup at higher cost; capex programme experiences delays/overruns (Southland Wind Farm precedent) extending the growth-capex tail through the full 10-year horizon rather than tapering to near-zero. Terminal value: Gordon growth (7,245.1) binds ahead of the 10.5x EBITDAF cap (9,457.8).

base.cap_terminal_value_formula: terminal_cap_multiple x Y10 adj_ebitdaf (NOT owner FCF)
base.implied_exit_multiple_basis: EV/EBITDAF (Y10 terminal_value / Y10 adj_ebitdaf) -- comparable to CEN's own historical EV/underlying-EBITDAF multiples

bull.cap_terminal_value_formula: terminal_cap_multiple x Y10 adj_ebitdaf (NOT owner FCF)
bull.implied_exit_multiple_basis: EV/EBITDAF (Y10 terminal_value / Y10 adj_ebitdaf) -- comparable to CEN's own historical EV/underlying-EBITDAF multiples

bear.cap_terminal_value_formula: terminal_cap_multiple x Y10 adj_ebitdaf (NOT owner FCF)
bear.implied_exit_multiple_basis: EV/EBITDAF (Y10 terminal_value / Y10 adj_ebitdaf) -- comparable to CEN's own historical EV/underlying-EBITDAF multiples

base.note: Entry price sits well below intrinsic value because base-case growth (2.0-4.5% revenue) is far below the 15% IRR hurdle -- this is the expected, mathematically consistent result for a low-growth yield stock, not a modeling error (Step 4 sanity property: entry price approaches IV only as growth approaches the hurdle rate).
base.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

sensitivity.note: Corrected matrix: the terminal cap now applies to Y10 EBITDAF (not Y10 owner FCF), so Gordon growth binds across most of the WACC/terminal-growth grid (real sensitivity to terminal growth is now visible) and the 12.5x EBITDAF cap only binds at the low-WACC/high-growth corner (WACC<=7.3% with growth>=2.2%, and WACC=6.3% across the whole growth range), where it correctly prevents the Gordon formula's WACC-minus-g denominator from blowing up the valuation.

sanity_check.correction_applied_2026_08_09: Fixed terminal-value bug: exit-multiple cap now applies to Y10 EBITDAF (adj_ebitdaf), not Y10 owner FCF, per Step 8c.5 (min(gordon_tv, exit_multiple_cap x terminal_ebitda)). Base IV moved $4.99 -> $6.36; bull $8.44 -> $11.28; bear $1.90 -> $2.57; weighted $5.08 -> $6.65.

1_implied_pe_far_above_historical_avg.detail: BASE implied P/E (19.46x) remains BELOW the FY22-25 historical average (33.13x). BULL implied P/E (34.51x) is essentially AT the historical average (33.13x) and well below the FY2023 peak (49.69x) -- no trip on P/E in any scenario.

2_implied_pb_far_above_historical_avg.detail: BASE implied P/B (1.51x) remains below the historical average (2.4x). BULL implied P/B (2.68x) is essentially AT the all-time historical high (2.71x, FY2025) -- a mild trip: the bull case assumes the market will pay a book-value multiple at the very top of CEN's own 4-year range, on top of an enlarged (post-Manawa, post-raise) equity base. Not extreme, but flagged.

3_implied_ev_ebitdaf_far_above_historica.detail: BASE implied EV/EBITDAF (9.4x on FY26 guidance) remains below the historical average (12.84x) and below the current market multiple (12.37x). BULL implied EV/EBITDAF (14.78x) exceeds CEN's own historical MAXIMUM (13.49x, FY2023) by ~1.3x -- this IS a trip: the bull case's terminal multiple (13.5x) is already at the top of history, and layering the bull case's above-consensus near-term growth AND margin expansion on top of that terminal multiple pushes the near-term implied multiple beyond anything CEN has traded at. This is judged ACCEPTABLE, not auto-fixed, because: (a) it applies only to the bull scenario (25% weight), which is explicitly designed to represent a favourable-outcomes tail, not the central case; (b) the terminal EXIT multiple itself (13.5x) is NOT above history -- only the near-term implied multiple is elevated, because bull-case FCF is temporarily depressed by the same capex supercycle as the other scenarios; (c) the base and probability-weighted cases, which drive the headline conclusion, are NOT tripped.

4_price_top_decile_with_large_upside.detail: Price ($9.08) IS in the top decile of the 10-year range ($4.66-$9.63). BASE case now produces -29.9% (downside) -- condition does not apply to base. BEAR produces -71.6% (downside) -- does not apply. BULL now produces +24.3% (upside) at this top-decile price -- condition IS live for bull. Evaluated: the bull case's assumptions (above-consensus electrification demand, full Manawa synergy capture, benign EA reform outcome, faster capex taper, lower WACC) are a coherent, internally-consistent set of favourable-but-plausible outcomes, not a mechanical artifact -- and even so, the bull IV ($11.28) implies only +24.3% upside, a modest re-rating relative to the current price, not an extreme one. Given trip conditions 2 and 3 also flagged the bull case's near-term implied multiples as being at/above CEN's historical maximum, the bull case is retained as reported but explicitly flagged as the upper end of a plausible range rather than a base-rate expectation -- consistent with its 25% probability weight.

sanity_check.diagnosis: PARTIAL TRIP (bull scenario only; base and probability-weighted results pass cleanly). After correcting the terminal-value bug (exit multiple now applied to Y10 EBITDAF, not Y10 owner FCF), the BASE case ($6.36, -29.9%) and BEAR case ($2.57, -71.6%) both remain solidly conservative versus history on every implied multiple (P/E, P/B, EV/EBITDAF, P/S all below their FY22-25 averages), and Gordon growth -- not the terminal cap -- is now the binding constraint in both scenarios, confirming the cap is functioning as a backstop rather than the primary driver. The BULL case ($11.28, +24.3%) is the one scenario where the terminal EBITDAF cap (13.5x) binds ahead of Gordon growth, and its resulting implied near-term EV/EBITDAF multiple (14.78x on FY26 guidance) modestly exceeds CEN's own all-time-high historical multiple (13.49x, FY2023) -- a genuine but moderate trip on conditions 2-4, confined to the bull scenario. No automatic fix was applied because: the trip is proportionate to how the bull case is deliberately constructed (best-case demand + margin + capital-efficiency + WACC assumptions stacked together), it does not touch the base case that anchors the headline conclusion, and the probability-weighted IV ($6.65, -26.8%) remains firmly in downside territory. The overall conclusion is unchanged from the pre-correction analysis in direction (Contact is separately priced by the market on a forward EV/EBITDAF basis broadly in line with its own history, while a disciplined owner-FCF DCF that fully charges the ongoing capex supercycle produces a lower base-case value) but the magnitude of the gap has narrowed materially (base case moved from -45.1% to -29.9% after the fix).
sanity_check.fix_applied: Terminal-value MECHANICAL bug fixed (cap now applies to Y10 EBITDAF, not Y10 owner FCF) -- this was a genuine coding defect, not an assumption tuned to a target. No further assumption changes were made post-fix; the bull-case multiple trip (conditions 2-4) was evaluated and judged proportionate/acceptable given its scope (bull-only, 25% weight) and is documented rather than papered over by re-tuning bull assumptions.
sanity_check.valuation_philosophy: This DCF intentionally diverges from the current market price in the base and bear cases, and lands close to (moderately above) it in the bull case. Contact Energy is being valued here as a capital-intensive, debt-funded growth-capex program mid-cycle: owner FCF is heavily depressed today (Y1 owner-FCF margin ~8.3% base case) by ~$380-510m/yr of combined stay-in-business + growth capex against ~$965m of EBITDAF, and only reaches a mature, capital-light margin (~17.8% base case) by around Year 8-10 as the Te Mihi Stage 2 / Glenbrook / Kowhai Park / Glorit build programme completes and growth capex tapers to near-zero. The market, by contrast, appears to be capitalizing forward EBITDAF directly at a multiple in line with CEN's own trading history (~12.4x FY26 guidance vs. a 12.84x FY23-25 average) -- a methodology that does not explicitly deduct the capex needed to sustain and grow that EBITDAF. Both views are internally consistent; they simply answer different questions (EBITDAF-multiple = 'what would a buyer of the EBITDAF stream pay today', owner-FCF DCF = 'what is left for equity holders after funding the capex that produces that EBITDAF'). After correcting the terminal-value mechanic, the base-case gap to the market price narrows to a more moderate -29.9% (from an erroneous -45.1%), and the bull case now clears the current price entirely (+24.3%), showing the valuation is genuinely sensitive to whether the capex programme converts efficiently into durable free cash flow. Investors comfortable that it will (i.e., that the market's implicit EBITDAF-multiple read is closer to correct) should weight the bull/base blend more heavily; investors skeptical (regulatory risk, dry-year hydrology, gas scarcity, delay/overrun risk as seen at Southland Wind Farm) should weight bear/base more heavily. The probability-weighted IV of $6.65 (-26.8%) reflects a 50% base weighting that still shows meaningful downside even after the correction -- this stock's current valuation continues to be supported more by yield-seeking demand and EBITDAF-multiple continuity than by a discounted owner-FCF case, though less dramatically so than before the fix.
sanity_check.passed_note: PASSED at the base-case/probability-weighted level (which anchors the headline conclusion). Two of four trip conditions fired in SCOPE-LIMITED form on the bull scenario only (see trip_conditions detail) -- documented, not silently waved through, and not auto-fixed because they reflect the bull case's deliberately optimistic assumption stack rather than a modeling defect.

fcf_quality_memo.note: Reported FCF is entirely dominated by the timing of growth capex (FY2025 growth capex $363m vs stay-in-business capex $110m), not by underlying earnings quality. FY2023's -$190m and FY2024's $0m reflect the Tauhara/Te Huka 3 geothermal build peak, not a deterioration in the operating business (underlying EBITDAF grew every year: $576m FY23 -> $663m FY24 -> $774m FY25).
fcf_quality_memo.sbc_adjustment: SBC ($4-5m/yr, ~0.15% of revenue) is immaterial for CEN -- unlike SBC-heavy tech/growth names, it is not a material driver of the reported-vs-owner FCF gap. The dominant adjustment for this ticker is the capex taper (Step 1c) and the terminal-value mechanic (Step 4/8c.5), not the SBC adjustment (Step 1b).
fcf_quality_memo.if_sbc_treated_as_non_cash_memo: Adding back the ~$5m/yr SBC would move FY2025 owner FCF from $67m to $72m (reported) -- a ~7% difference, immaterial to the overall valuation given the dominant capex-timing and terminal-value effects.
fcf_quality_memo.deferred_revenue_in_ocf: Not applicable -- Contact is a utility/gentailer, not a subscription business; no material deferred-revenue working-capital dynamic.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Contact is valued as a capital-intensive NZ utility mid-way through a growth-capex supercycle, not as a growth compounder. The model is a 10-year component-built owner-FCF DCF that charges growth capex in full as it is spent and lets it taper as the renewable build programme (Tauhara, Te Huka 3, Te Mihi Stage 2, Kowhai Park solar, Glenbrook-Ohurua battery) converts into EBITDAF.
valuation_philosophy.why_iv_below_price: The market prices CEN on a forward EV/EBITDAF basis (~12.4x FY26 guidance, in line with its own FY23-25 history of 12.84x), which does not explicitly penalise the cash currently being consumed by growth capex. A disciplined owner-FCF DCF does. Both approaches agree on the appropriate EXIT multiple; they disagree on who pays for the build. That gap -- not a mechanical miscalibration -- is the -29.9% base-case downside.
valuation_philosophy.normalisation: Anchored on UNDERLYING FY2025 earnings (EBITDAF $774m, profit $261m), excluding the one-off non-cash $98m Ahuroa Gas Storage onerous-contract provision release that inflated reported EBITDAF to $872m and profit to $331m.
valuation_philosophy.acquisition_treatment: Manawa Energy completed 11 July 2025 (FY2026), so H1-2026 consolidates Manawa and 75%-owned King Country Energy and is NOT organically comparable to H1-2025. Per-share history spanning the deal is not meaningful: shares went 798.5m -> 994.4m on scrip, plus ~60m from the Feb-2026 NZ$525m raise (1,054.4m used). Net debt uses the 31-Dec-2025 balance sheet with the post-balance-date raise proceeds added to cash.
valuation_philosophy.terminal_value: min(Gordon growth, exit multiple x Y10 EBITDAF), with the exit multiple anchored to CEN's own FY2023-25 EV/underlying-EBITDAF history (base 12.5x vs 12.84x actual). Gordon binds in base and bear; the cap binds only in bull.
valuation_philosophy.investment_framing: This is a yield-plus-modest-growth bond proxy (dividends 35->39 cps), not a multi-bagger. At $9.08 -- top decile of the 10-year $4.66-$9.63 range -- the base case says the market has already capitalised the growth programme's future earnings while an owner-FCF view is still paying for it. The bull case ($11.28) requires electrification demand above the MBIE reference case, benign Electricity Authority reform, and an on-schedule capital-efficient build.
valuation_philosophy.known_limitation: The bull case trips three of four Step 8c conditions (implied P/B 2.68x, EV/EBITDAF 14.8x on FY26 guidance, and upside at a top-decile price). It is retained at 25% weight and documented rather than re-tuned; readers should treat the bull IV as an optimistic bound, not a target.
